stem:
Asparagine and valine are two naturally occurring amino acids.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Give the molecular formula of asparagine.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Name all of the functional groups in an asparagine molecule.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Draw the structure of the dipeptide formed by valine and asparagine.

The peptide bond should be shown displayed and should be clearly labelled.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: A solution of valine in water acts as a buffer solution.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a buffer solution.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Write two equations to explain how valine can act as a buffer. Use the formula $\text{H}_2\text{NCHRCO}_2\text{H}$ for valine in your equations.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Each valine molecule has one chiral carbon atom.

Draw three-dimensional diagrams to show the two optical isomers of valine. The $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}$ group can be represented as R.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Asparagine is hydrolysed when heated with aqueous sulfuric acid.

Write an equation for this reaction.
